options.B: Going on a date with Patrick

distraction.A: The scenery at Fairy Bay is delightful.
distraction.B: Patrick Redfern was utterly enchanted by Mrs. Marshall.

reasoning: Poirot told Marshall that he should not tell anyone that he had seen her.
Patrick Redford also arrived, and it was clear that he was looking for Elena Marshall as well.
Poirot said that Elena Marshall was not a woman who liked to be alone, she only lived in the admiration of men.
Based on this inference, Elena Marshall's visit to Elven Bay must have been to meet someone, and this person is not Patrick Redford.

questions.question: The clues on Linda's fireplace mantel show that ( )

options.A: Someone was cooking in the room.
options.B: Someone wants to burn the evidence of the ritual
options.D: Room usage time is too long.

distraction.D: The fireplace mantle has been burning

reasoning: Linda hates Mrs. Marshall and has thoughts of killing her.
Linda was reading in the bookstore, putting back books she didn't like, and then picked up a small book with a brown leather cover that she was holding, lost in time while reading it.
The room contains melted wax from burnt candles, scraps of green paper or cardstock, and scribbled words '…and so on…', along with a common needle, remnants of burned animal material, possibly hair.

On the left side of the fireplace, there is a shelf with a row of books. There is a Bible, an old collection of Shakespeare's plays, "The Marriage of William Ash" written by Lady Hume, "Younger Sister" by Charlotte Yong, "The Young Persons of Shropshire" by Charlotte Yong, "The Cathedral Murder" by T.S. Eliot, "Saint Joan" by George Bernard Shaw, "Gone with the Wind" by Margaret Mitchell, and "The Burning Court" by Dashiell Hammett, all of which are about stepmothers.

Poirot discovered that there was another book inserted between these pages, a smaller one with a brown leather cover, inscribed with the words, 'I was right... Yes, I was right, but the other thing – could it possibly be true? No, impossible, unless...'
Poirot discovered that the small book with the brown leather cover was titled "The History of Sorcery and Invisible Poison"

Based on the clues, Linda does not like Mrs. Marshall, the books in the room are about stepmothers, she has bought books on witchcraft to study methods of murder, and there are wax and needles, hair, etc. in the fireplace. Therefore, the items burned in the fireplace are evidence that Linda was practicing witchcraft to kill Mrs. Marshall.

questions.question: The murderer of Mrs. Marshall is ( ).

distraction.B: Mr. Marshall met with Mrs. Marshall and Patrick Redford for a date.
distraction.C: Elena Marshall was speaking to a person who was threatening her the day before.
distraction.D: Mrs. Gardner hinted that Miss Darnley was very fond of Mr. Marshall.

reasoning: Patrick Redford expresses his deep love for Elena.
Mrs. Marshall has a lot of property.

Alice Corey was strangled to death in the Caisarine of Black Mountain, where she married Edward Corey against the objections of her relatives and took out a life insurance policy with him as the beneficiary. She spent a considerable amount of money on the policy.
A jogging physical education teacher, Kristen Davila, provided an alibi for Edward Caulkin.
The Redfern couple were identified by Surrey police as Edward Colgate and Christine DeVere.

Miss Bustle said that Mrs. Redfever's fear of heights was even worse than hers. A few days ago, on the cliff-top path to Harford, Mrs. Redfever was so dizzy and disoriented that she clung to Miss Bustle tightly.
Christine Redfern carelessly ran across the narrow footbridge.

Based on the above clues, Patrick Redfern approached Mrs. Marshall only to deceive her for money, as Patrick Redfern had previously murdered his wife and Redfern's wife provided an alibi for him. This case is very similar to the previous one. Additionally, Christine Redfern claimed to be afraid of heights but could run across a narrow footbridge without concern, indicating that she was lying. Therefore, it can be inferred that Patrick and Christine Redfern killed Mrs. Marshall.
